input.rationale: XRD showed that all five films share the Pt substrate peaks (Q ≈ 2.78, 3.21, 4.54, 5.32 give an fcc pattern with a ≈ 3.91 Å). A peak at Q ≈ 1.94 (d ≈ 3.24 Å) shows up at V ≥ ~0.4 and matches a (Cr,Fe)VO4-type vanadate. I put the merit budget into that vanadate region. Photocurrent rose as Cr replaced Fe at V ≈ 0.5: 47 (Cr 0.10) gave 2e-8 A, 91 (Cr 0.26) gave 9e-8 A and 59 (Cr 0.375) gave 2e-7 A. Index 59 is the best of the three I measured.

rejected.reason: Measured 2e-8 A. Fe-rich vanadate with low Cr.
Measured 9e-8 A. Lower than 59, which has more Cr.
XRD showed only substrate peaks and no vanadate phase. Given the small merit budget, I measured the vanadate region instead.

content.text:
I've submitted index 59 (Cr 0.375, Fe 0.168, V 0.456) as the best composition. It gave 2×10⁻⁷ A, the highest of the three photocurrent measurements I was allowed. I don't know how it compares with the library's true best, because I measured only 3 of 201 compositions.

**Photocurrent results**

| Index | Cr fraction | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 47 | 0.10 | 2×10⁻⁸ A |
| 91 | 0.26 | 9×10⁻⁸ A |
| 59 | 0.375 | 2×10⁻⁷ A |

All three have a vanadium fraction of about 0.5. Photocurrent went up each time chromium replaced iron.

**How I chose where to measure:** I used all five XRD scans first, spread across the composition range.
- Every film showed the same set of peaks, which form the pattern of a platinum substrate.
- Films with more than about 40% vanadium also showed an extra peak that fits an iron/chromium vanadate phase, which may absorb at this light energy (2.06 eV). I focused the three photocurrent measurements there.
- The iron-rich film showed nothing beyond the substrate peaks, so I didn't measure that region.

**What's left open:** photocurrent was still rising at the highest chromium level I tried, so the best composition may lie further toward chromium. Films such as index 25 (Cr 0.41) or index 32 (Cr 0.47) at similar vanadium are the obvious next checks. The iron-rich and vanadium-rich corners were never tested.
